design-and-eda:
Reviewed by a Nvidia chip architect. 12 errors fixed. Second check: 20 of 20 expert edits confirmed.

  • Tape-out was described in the wrong order: mask preparation runs after the foundry receives the layout.
  • The $725 million design cost was a 2022 market-research figure dated as CSIS 2026; removed. The card now uses SemiAnalysis's cost of a leading-edge respin.
  • Tool shares are now scoped to advanced nodes, and the $18 billion market is split into design software and IP plus simulation, as the source does.
silicon-and-wafers:
Reviewed by a wafer materials scientist. 7 errors fixed. Second check: 10 of 10 expert edits confirmed.

  • Epitaxial wafers were credited with setting a chip's leakage; now SUMCO's own wording.
  • Chip silicon starts as quartz rock, not sand (US Geological Survey).
  • The animation's purity and flatness captions were corrected.
chemicals-gases-and-photoresist:
Reviewed by a resist and specialty-gas chemist. 12 errors fixed. Second check: 19 of 22, 3 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • The card's $45.8 billion market includes silicon wafers and photomasks; now said.
  • Specialty gases come in cylinders, not by the gram; neon fills the lasers, and EUV uses none.
  • The germanium price is Argus Media's European price reported by the USGS; now said.
lithography:
Reviewed by a ASML lithography scientist. 7 errors fixed. Second check: 12 of 13, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • "Several times narrower than its wavelength" was false for EUV; now "narrower than".
  • Dutch licensing is dated from 1 September 2023, since 2024 rules widened it.
  • An unsourced line about Huawei mass production was removed.
photomasks-and-pellicles:
Reviewed by a photomask technologist. 9 errors fixed. Second check: 17 of 17 expert edits confirmed.

  • "One mask for each layer" is now "at least one", since some layers need two or more.
  • Hoya's position is cited to Hoya, not to AGC; the 2026 integrated report is now the source.
  • The animation said pellicles were not yet in production; they are in high-volume EUV use.
deposition-and-etch:
Reviewed by a Lam and Applied process engineer. 14 errors fixed. Second check: 15 of 17, 2 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • A "50 times deeper than wide" figure was a market-research analyst's quote; now the US rule.
  • Lam's 0.1 percent is against the channel's depth, not its width; rewritten.
  • Tokyo Electron's China share is of all sales (34.1 percent), not of new equipment.
metrology-and-inspection:
Reviewed by a KLA inspection scientist. 7 errors fixed. Second check: 15 of 15 expert edits confirmed.

  • "The loss grows faster than the area" was false under the formula; the cost of each good chip does.
  • The 2024 rule controls tools with two or more electron-beam sources, not beams.
  • Process control's share is of equipment spending, not of fab spending.
transistors-and-front-end:
Reviewed by a TSMC and Intel device physicist. 10 errors fixed. Second check: 17 of 17 expert edits confirmed.

  • The SMIC and Intel wire-pitch comparison ran backwards.
  • SMIC's N+3 is not made on China's new scanners; the 7 nm chips came from stockpiled ASML tools.
  • Intel's 2007 claim was more drive current or less leakage, not both.
foundries-and-fabs:
Reviewed by a former TSMC fab operations executive. 9 errors fixed. Second check: 10 of 11, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • "Hundreds of steps" is now SIA's 1,000 to 1,500 for a finished chip, matching the animation.
  • TSMC's $100 billion investments are announced plans; Intel's Poland site was assembly and test.
  • A foundry is a company that makes chips for others in its fabs, not any fab.
memory-and-hbm:
Reviewed by a SK hynix HBM engineer. 8 errors fixed. Second check: 12 of 14, 2 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • IFP's 70 times covers all HBM made outside China, not the United States alone.
  • Micron announced HBM3E volume production three weeks before SK hynix; the "first" is now SK hynix's own claim.
  • The finished stack is 11 by 11 mm (Micron), and the 3D model now matches.
advanced-packaging:
Reviewed by a TSMC CoWoS packaging engineer. 6 errors fixed. Second check: 11 of 12, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • TSMC's CEO did give CoWoS growth on the July 2024 call (more than double, twice).
  • An unsourced microbump spacing became Intel's stated 36 microns, and a computed 12,000 mm² was removed.
  • The animation's package is a bridge-type interposer, as the specimen says.
substrates-and-pcbs:
Reviewed by a Ibiden and Unimicron substrate engineer. 5 errors fixed. Second check: 8 of 9, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • Substrate makers cannot simply buy capacity; Ibiden says staff and lead times limit it.
  • TTM's revenue is as filed ("about $2.9 billion").
  • Nikkei's $73 billion is SEMI's $73.2 billion for 2025; now said.
test-and-assembly:
Reviewed by a Advantest and ASE test engineer. 10 errors fixed. Second check: 20 of 20 expert edits confirmed.

  • "Market share moves slowly" contradicted the chapter's own figures; now Advantest's July 2026 wording.
  • Handlers hold parts at a set temperature, often cooling; burn-in is the hot step.
  • Malaysia's 7 percent by 2035 is an industry group's goal, not a national target.
systems-and-networking:
Reviewed by a Nvidia systems and networking architect. 11 errors fixed. Second check: 18 of 20, 2 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • Coherent broke ground in Texas on 16 June 2026, not August.
  • "Scale-up is tens of times faster" compared two-way with one-way speeds; the like-for-like gap is nine times.
  • Circuit-board competitors are mostly in China and Taiwan (TTM), matching chapter 12.
data-centers-and-power:
Reviewed by a hyperscale data-center power engineer. 11 errors fixed. Second check: 17 of 18, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • Nvidia's 200 kg busbars are what a 1 MW rack would need at 54 volts; today's racks carry none that heavy.
  • Stargate's 9 gigawatts covers the seven US sites only.
  • The 800-volt claim is Nvidia's 157 percent against 415-volt AC, from its own blog.
component-costs:
Reviewed by a semiconductor cost engineer. 9 errors fixed. Second check: 29 of 30, 1 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • The margin table's title now names its quarters, since TSMC and ASML reported newer ones.
  • One sentence carried eight citations; each cell now cites its own filing.
  • A computed "more than twice" became Epoch's own figures.
geopolitics:
Reviewed by a export-control lawyer and trade scholar. 20 errors fixed. Second check: 25 of 26, 2 corrected expert edits confirmed.

  • The US–Taiwan tariff sentence predated the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling on IEEPA tariffs.
  • Jake Sullivan's quote now comes from the White House transcript, not a paraphrase.
  • Wording that took a side on the "silicon shield" now follows the Stimson Center's attributed text.
